description: Convert any Gregorian calendar date to its Julian Day Number and back, using the standard astronomical algorithm.

faqs.a: The Julian Day Number counts days since noon on January 1, 4713 BC (Julian proleptic calendar). Astronomers use it to compute intervals between dates simply.
faqs.q: What is a Julian Day Number?

faqs.a: Use the standard algorithm: JDN = (1461×(y+4800+(m−14)/12))/4 + … (integer division). The tool computes it exactly.
Yes — both directions are supported: date → JDN and JDN → date.
faqs.q: Can I convert a JDN back to a date?

howto: Enter a calendar date to get its Julian Day Number.
Or enter a Julian Day Number to get the calendar date.
Use the JDN to compute exact day differences.
title: Julian Date Converter
